evals.name: A full diagnosis in Claude Code
evals.prompt: I'm in Claude Code. Evaluate skills/draft-cognitive-interview-script before I open the PR.
evals.expected_output: The evaluator reads only the description and the case prompts first and writes a cold case, then runs the validator, judges triggering next to the catalog's other descriptions, and runs three cases with and without the skill using fresh agents. It ends with the one-screen report, verdict first.
assertions: Writes a cold case, or says it will, before reading the body of the skill.
Runs or plans each case twice: with the skill and with no skill.
Does not run the API script without showing the number of calls and asking first.
The report opens with a verdict that is one of: ready, fix first, could not test.
The report has the parts Structure, Triggering, On the job, What to fix, and How this was run.
Does not edit the skill.

evals.name: No tools
evals.prompt:
I'm on Claude Desktop, no code execution. Here is my skill as pasted text: the SKILL.md and evals/evals.json for decompose-comb-barriers. Is it any good?

---
name: decompose-comb-barriers
description: Use when one behavior is defined (who does what, when) and the question is why people are not doing it, or when a team is about to pick an intervention without naming the barrier it addresses. Lists competing capability, opportunity, and motivation hypotheses, each with a question that could rule it out, and ranks them. Do not use when the goal is still vague; use define-key-behavior. Not for choosing what to do about a confirmed barrier; use select-intervention-levers.
---
[the rest of SKILL.md and the four test cases follow]
evals.expected_output: The evaluator works in the conversation and keeps the order: from the description and the case prompts alone it writes a cold case and its own bare answers before using the skill's body. It walks the checklist in place of the validator, and its report says the result is indicative and was run in conversation on one model.
assertions: Writes its answer to at least one case without the skill before producing the answer with the skill.
Says the comparison is indicative because it was run in one conversation.
Uses the checklist, or says the validator could not be run.
Gives triggering as counts in words, not as precision and recall decimals.
The report's last part says how it was run and that the preference is a model's judgment.

evals.name: Not skill evaluation
evals.prompt: Can you evaluate our maternal health chatbot? We want to know if it's improving outcomes.
evals.expected_output: The evaluator says this is evaluation of an AI product and a program outcome, which it does not do, and points to The Agency Fund's evaluation playbook. It runs no checks.
assertions: Says it evaluates library skills and not AI products or program outcomes.
Points to The Agency Fund's evaluation playbook.
Runs no checks and produces no diagnosis.

evals.name: A meta-skill
evals.prompt: Run the evaluator on besci-navigator. I changed how it opens and want to know if it still does its job.
evals.expected_output: The evaluator says a meta-skill is checked on frontmatter, files, test cases, and changelog only, takes triggering requests from its test cases and near-misses it writes, and judges the first turn of the interview against the bare model.
assertions: Says the eight-section rules do not apply to a meta-skill.
Compares the skill's answers with answers written with no skill.
Judges a single turn of the interview and does not expect a full output.
The report opens with a verdict.

evals.name: After a model release
evals.prompt: A new Claude model was released this week. Which of our published skills got worse? We have twelve skills in the repo.
evals.expected_output: The evaluator proposes the script for this, since it needs repeated runs on two models across twelve skills, shows how to get the call count with --dry-run, and asks for the go-ahead before spending. It does not start the runs.
assertions: Recommends the script and names the two models to compare.
Shows or offers the dry run and its call count before any API call.
Asks for the go-ahead before spending.
Says results per skill will be reported separately for each model.
